instruction: Using Visual Studio Code, create a Python script named `worldbank_india_energy_emission_analysis.py` inside `/home/user/analysis_results/worldbank_data/`. First, open Google Chrome and navigate to `https://datahelpdesk.worldbank.org/knowledgebase/articles/889392-about-the-indicators-api-documentation`. From this, determine how to correctly form API requests. Then, construct and fetch data from two World Bank API endpoints for India: (1) Energy use (indicator `EG.USE.PCAP.KG.OE`), and (2) CO2 emissions per capita (indicator `EN.ATM.CO2E.PC`). Use `requests` to retrieve data from both endpoints, handling pagination if necessary. Extract the last 10 available years with both values, align them by year, and create a DataFrame with columns: `year`, `energy_use`, and `co2_emission`. Compute: (a) the Pearson correlation between energy use and CO2 emissions, and (b) the year showing the sharpest percentage drop in CO2 emissions relative to its previous year. Save both results to a text file named `india_energy_emission_summary.txt` formatted as: `Correlation: <value>, Sharpest_Emission_Drop_Year: <year>`.
